These instructions show you the steps to connect to the Selling Partner API (SP-API). For links to additional examples, refer to SP-API SDKs .
Before your application can connect to SP-API, you must:
Register the application. For details, refer to Registering your application .
Get the application authorized by a selling partner or, if you're a private developer , authorize it yourself. For details, refer to Authorizing Selling Partner API applications .
Step 1. Request a Login with Amazon access token
A Login with Amazon (LWA) access token authorizes your application to take certain actions on behalf of a selling partner . An LWA access token expires one hour after it is issued.

An LWA access token must be included in calls to all operations except restricted operation s, which return Personally Identifiable Information (PII). When calling restricted operations, instead of including an LWA access token, you include a Restricted Data Token (RDT). For information about getting RDTs and calling restricted operations, refer to the Tokens API Use Case Guide .
To request an LWA access token, make a secure HTTP POST to the LWA authentication server ( https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token ) with the following parameters:

Name Description Required grant_type The type of access grant requested. Values: - refresh_token . Use this for calling operations that require authorization from a selling partner. All operations that are not grantless operations require authorization from a selling partner. When specifying this value, include the refresh_token parameter. - client_credentials . Use this for calling grantless operations . When specifying this value, include the scope parameter. Yes refresh_token The LWA refresh token. Get this value when the selling partner authorizes your application. For more information, refer to Authorizing Selling Partner API applications . No. Include refresh_token for calling operations that require authorization from a selling partner. If you include refresh_token , do not include scope. scope The scope of the LWA authorization grant. Values:

No. Include scope for calling a grantless operation . If you include scope, do not include refresh_token . client_id Get this value when you register your application. Refer to Viewing your developer information . Yes client_secret Get this value when you register your application. Refer to Viewing your developer information . Yes
Example for calling an operation that requires selling partner authorization:

POST /auth/o2/token HTTP/l.l Host: api.amazon.com Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8 grant_type=refresh_token &refresh_token=Aztr|... &client_id=foodev &client_secret=Y76SDl2F
Example for calling a grantless operation :

POST /auth/o2/token HTTP/l.l Host: api.amazon.com Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8 grant_type=client_credentials &scope=sellingpartnerapi::notifications &client_id=foodev &client_secret=Y76SDl2F

To avoid getting an untrusted certificate authority (CA) error when calling the LWA authorization server, be sure to update your trust store so that your application trusts the LWA authorization server.
A successful response includes the following values.

Name Description access_token The LWA access token. Maximum size: 2048 bytes. token_type The type of token returned. Must be bearer . expires_in The number of seconds before the LWA access token becomes invalid. refresh_token The LWA refresh token that you submitted in the request. Maximum size: 2048 bytes.

HTTP/l.l 200 OK Content-Type: application/json;charset UTF-8 Cache-Control: no-store Pragma:no-cache { "access_token":"Atza|IQEBLjAsAhRmHjNgHpi0U-Dme37rR6CuUpSREXAMPLE", "token_type":"bearer", "expires_in":3600, "refresh_token":"Atzr|IQEBLzAtAhRPpMJxdwVz2Nn6f2y-tpJX2DeXEXAMPLE" }
For more information, visit the Authorization Code Grant page in the Login with Amazon documentation.
An SP-API URI contains the following components.

Name Description Example HTTP method The HTTP method. GET Endpoint An SP-API endpoint . https://sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com Path Resource location. /catalog/2022-04-01/items/{asin} Query string The query parameters. ?marketplaceIds=ATVPDKIKX0DER Path parameter The path parameters. EXAMPLEASIN
Step 3. Add headers to the URI
Add headers to the URI that you constructed in Step 2. Construct a Selling Partner API URI . Here are the HTTP headers to include in requests to the SP-API:

Name Description host the Amazon store endpoint. Refer to SP-API endpoints . x-amz-access-token The LWA access token. Refer to Step 1. Request a Login with Amazon access token . Note about restricted operations. If you call a restricted operation, pass in an RDT here instead of an LWA access token. For information about getting RDTs and calling restricted operations, refer to the Tokens API Use Case Guide in the Tokens API Use Case Guide. x-amz-date The date and time of your request. user-agent Your application name, application version number, platform, and programming language. You must include a user-agent header in every request to the SP-API. • Maximum length: 500 characters. • Minimum required information: App name, version, and language. • Optional: You can add additional attributes separated by semicolons. How to assemble a user-agent header Concatenate the following information: • Application name • Forward slash • Application version • Space • Opening parenthesis • Language name/value pair • Closing parentheses Escape the following characters with a blackslash: • Backslash. • Forward slash in the application name. • Opening parenthesis in the application version. • Equal sign in the attribute name. • Closing parenthesis and semicolon in attribute values. Examples: • AppId/AppVersionId (Language=LanguageNameAndOptionallyVersion) • MySellingTool/2.0 (Language=Java/1.8.0.221; Platform=Windows/10) • MyCompany/build16 (Language=Perl; Host=my.desktop.example.com)
The following example shows how to call the SP-API with a URI and headers but no signing information:

GET /catalog/2022-04-01/items/EXAMPLEASIN?marketplaceIds=ATVPDKIKX0DER HTTP/1.1 host: sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com user-agent: My Selling Tool/2.0 (Language=Java/1.8.0.221; Platform=Windows/10) x-amz-access-token=Atza|IQEBLjAsAhRmHjNgHpi0U-Dme37rR6CuUpSREXAMPLE x-amz-date: 20190430T123600Z

These instructions show you the steps to connect to the Selling Partner API (SP-API). For links to additional examples, refer to SP-API SDKs.

Prerequisites

Before your application can connect to SP-API, you must:

  • Register the application. For details, refer to Registering your application.
  • Get the application authorized by a selling partner or, if you're a private developer, authorize it yourself. For details, refer to Authorizing Selling Partner API applications.

Step 1. Request a Login with Amazon access token

A Login with Amazon (LWA) access token authorizes your application to take certain actions on behalf of a selling partner. An LWA access token expires one hour after it is issued.

📘

Note

An LWA access token must be included in calls to all operations except restricted operations, which return Personally Identifiable Information (PII). When calling restricted operations, instead of including an LWA access token, you include a Restricted Data Token (RDT). For information about getting RDTs and calling restricted operations, refer to the Tokens API Use Case Guide.

To request an LWA access token, make a secure HTTP POST to the LWA authentication server (https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token) with the following parameters:

NameDescriptionRequired
grant_typeThe type of access grant requested. Values:
- refresh_token. Use this for calling operations that require authorization from a selling partner. All operations that are not grantless operations require authorization from a selling partner. When specifying this value, include the refresh_token parameter.
- client_credentials. Use this for calling grantless operations. When specifying this value, include the scope parameter.		Yes
refresh_tokenThe LWA refresh token. Get this value when the selling partner authorizes your application. For more information, refer to Authorizing Selling Partner API applications.No. Include refresh_token for calling operations that require authorization from a selling partner. If you include refresh_token, do not include scope.
scopeThe scope of the LWA authorization grant. Values:
  • Notifications API: sellingpartnerapi::notifications
  • Application Management API: sellingpartnerapi::client_credential:rotation
  • Tracking API: sellingpartnerapi::shipments:track
No. Include scope for calling a grantless operation. If you include scope, do not include refresh_token.
client_idGet this value when you register your application. Refer to Viewing your developer information.Yes
client_secretGet this value when you register your application. Refer to Viewing your developer information.Yes

Example for calling an operation that requires selling partner authorization:

POST /auth/o2/token HTTP/l.l
Host: api.amazon.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8
grant_type=refresh_token
&refresh_token=Aztr|...
&client_id=foodev
&client_secret=Y76SDl2F

Example for calling a grantless operation:

POST /auth/o2/token HTTP/l.l
Host: api.amazon.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8
grant_type=client_credentials
&scope=sellingpartnerapi::notifications
&client_id=foodev
&client_secret=Y76SDl2F
⭐

Tip

To avoid getting an untrusted certificate authority (CA) error when calling the LWA authorization server, be sure to update your trust store so that your application trusts the LWA authorization server.

A successful response includes the following values.

NameDescription
access_tokenThe LWA access token. Maximum size: 2048 bytes.
token_typeThe type of token returned. Must be bearer.
expires_inThe number of seconds before the LWA access token becomes invalid.
refresh_tokenThe LWA refresh token that you submitted in the request. Maximum size: 2048 bytes.
HTTP/l.l 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json;charset UTF-8
Cache-Control: no-store
Pragma:no-cache
{
 "access_token":"Atza|IQEBLjAsAhRmHjNgHpi0U-Dme37rR6CuUpSREXAMPLE",
 "token_type":"bearer",
 "expires_in":3600,
 "refresh_token":"Atzr|IQEBLzAtAhRPpMJxdwVz2Nn6f2y-tpJX2DeXEXAMPLE"
}

For more information, visit the Authorization Code Grant page in the Login with Amazon documentation.

Step 2. Construct an SP-API URI

An SP-API URI contains the following components.

NameDescriptionExample
HTTP methodThe HTTP method.GET
EndpointAn SP-API endpoint.https://sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com
PathResource location./catalog/2022-04-01/items/{asin}
Query stringThe query parameters.?marketplaceIds=ATVPDKIKX0DER
Path parameterThe path parameters.EXAMPLEASIN

For example:

GET https://sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com/catalog/2022-04-01/items/EXAMPLEASIN?marketplaceIds=ATVPDKIKX0DER

Step 3. Add headers to the URI

Add headers to the URI that you constructed in Step 2. Construct a Selling Partner API URI. Here are the HTTP headers to include in requests to the SP-API:

NameDescription
hostthe Amazon store endpoint. Refer to SP-API endpoints.
x-amz-access-tokenThe LWA access token. Refer to Step 1. Request a Login with Amazon access token.
Note about restricted operations. If you call a restricted operation, pass in an RDT here instead of an LWA access token. For information about getting RDTs and calling restricted operations, refer to the Tokens API Use Case Guide in the Tokens API Use Case Guide.
x-amz-dateThe date and time of your request.
user-agentYour application name, application version number, platform, and programming language. You must include a user-agent header in every request to the SP-API.
• Maximum length: 500 characters.
• Minimum required information: App name, version, and language.
• Optional: You can add additional attributes separated by semicolons.
How to assemble a user-agent headerConcatenate the following information:
• Application name
• Forward slash
• Application version
• Space
• Opening parenthesis
• Language name/value pair
• Closing parentheses

Escape the following characters with a blackslash:
• Backslash.
• Forward slash in the application name.
• Opening parenthesis in the application version.
• Equal sign in the attribute name.
• Closing parenthesis and semicolon in attribute values.

Examples:
• AppId/AppVersionId (Language=LanguageNameAndOptionallyVersion)
• MySellingTool/2.0 (Language=Java/1.8.0.221; Platform=Windows/10)
• MyCompany/build16 (Language=Perl; Host=my.desktop.example.com)

The following example shows how to call the SP-API with a URI and headers but no signing information:

GET /catalog/2022-04-01/items/EXAMPLEASIN?marketplaceIds=ATVPDKIKX0DER HTTP/1.1
host: sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com
user-agent: My Selling Tool/2.0 (Language=Java/1.8.0.221;
Platform=Windows/10)
x-amz-access-token=Atza|IQEBLjAsAhRmHjNgHpi0U-Dme37rR6CuUpSREXAMPLE
x-amz-date: 20190430T123600Z

You must register as a Selling Partner API (SP-API) developer before you can register your Selling Partner API application .
The procedure for registering as a developer varies slightly depending on the type of application that you plan to create:

Private seller applications : Applications for sellers that are available only to your organization, and are self-authorized. Note that in Seller Central, you must have a professional selling account to develop SP-API private seller applications. Individual accounts are not eligible. You can upgrade your account to a professional plan at any time.
Private vendor applications : Vendor applications that are available only to your organization, and are self-authorized.

Public seller and vendor applications : Applications that are publicly available and are authorized by sellers or by vendors using OAuth. In accordance with the Solution Provider Portal Agreement , public developers must list their app in the Amazon Selling Partner Appstore.
Public and private applications are subject to authorization limits and restrictions. For more information, refer to Authorization Limits .
You must be a primary account user to complete registration.
Before you register, review the following information:
Policy requirements: Review the Acceptable Use Policy (AUP), Data Protection Policy (DPP), and Solution Provider Portal Agreement at Policies and Agreements .
Ensure that the tech team responsible for data security answers the security control questions of the developer profile application.
Review the Selling Partner API technical papers for detailed guidance on vulnerability management, network protection, and data encryption.
To understand key security controls for SP-API integration and how these controls relate to DPP provisions, see Key Security Control Guidance .
Website requirements: If you are registering as a public developer or service provider, ensure that your website meets the Website Guidelines for Public Developers and Service Providers .
Role selection: To understand which roles to request, review Selling Partner API Roles .
Application guidelines: Keep your developer profile application under the 500-word limit and write original content. Do not copy information from the AUP, DPP, or other Amazon policies.
Status tracking: For information about your registration status, refer to Developer Registration Request Status .
Profile updates: To learn how to update your developer profile, refer to Update Your Developer Profile in Solution Provider Portal .

You must register as a Selling Partner API (SP-API) developer before you can register your Selling Partner API application.

The procedure for registering as a developer varies slightly depending on the type of application that you plan to create:

  • Private seller applications: Applications for sellers that are available only to your organization, and are self-authorized. Note that in Seller Central, you must have a professional selling account to develop SP-API private seller applications. Individual accounts are not eligible. You can upgrade your account to a professional plan at any time.

  • Private vendor applications: Vendor applications that are available only to your organization, and are self-authorized.

  • Public seller and vendor applications: Applications that are publicly available and are authorized by sellers or by vendors using OAuth. In accordance with the Solution Provider Portal Agreement, public developers must list their app in the Amazon Selling Partner Appstore.

❗

Important

Public and private applications are subject to authorization limits and restrictions. For more information, refer to Authorization Limits.

You must be a primary account user to complete registration.

Registration resources

Before you register, review the following information:

  • Policy requirements: Review the Acceptable Use Policy (AUP), Data Protection Policy (DPP), and Solution Provider Portal Agreement at Policies and Agreements.

  • Security implementation:

    • Ensure that the tech team responsible for data security answers the security control questions of the developer profile application.
    • Review the Selling Partner API technical papers for detailed guidance on vulnerability management, network protection, and data encryption.
    • To understand key security controls for SP-API integration and how these controls relate to DPP provisions, see Key Security Control Guidance.

  • Website requirements: If you are registering as a public developer or service provider, ensure that your website meets the Website Guidelines for Public Developers and Service Providers.

  • Role selection: To understand which roles to request, review Selling Partner API Roles.

  • Application guidelines: Keep your developer profile application under the 500-word limit and write original content. Do not copy information from the AUP, DPP, or other Amazon policies.

  • Status tracking: For information about your registration status, refer to Developer Registration Request Status.

  • Profile updates: To learn how to update your developer profile, refer to Update Your Developer Profile in Solution Provider Portal.

d0:b575.text: These instructions show you the steps to connect to the Selling Partner API (SP-API). For links to additional examples, refer to SP-API SDKs .

d0:b577.text: Before your application can connect to SP-API, you must:

d0:b578.text: Register the application. For details, refer to Registering your application .

d0:b579.text: Get the application authorized by a selling partner or, if you're a private developer , authorize it yourself. For details, refer to Authorizing Selling Partner API applications .

d0:b580.text: Step 1. Request a Login with Amazon access token

d0:b581.text: A Login with Amazon (LWA) access token authorizes your application to take certain actions on behalf of a selling partner . An LWA access token expires one hour after it is issued.

d0:b584.text: An LWA access token must be included in calls to all operations except restricted operation s, which return Personally Identifiable Information (PII). When calling restricted operations, instead of including an LWA access token, you include a Restricted Data Token (RDT). For information about getting RDTs and calling restricted operations, refer to the Tokens API Use Case Guide .

d0:b585.text: To request an LWA access token, make a secure HTTP POST to the LWA authentication server ( https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token ) with the following parameters:

d0:b586.text: Name Description Required grant_type The type of access grant requested. Values: - refresh_token . Use this for calling operations that require authorization from a selling partner. All operations that are not grantless operations require authorization from a selling partner. When specifying this value, include the refresh_token parameter. - client_credentials . Use this for calling grantless operations . When specifying this value, include the scope parameter. Yes refresh_token The LWA refresh token. Get this value when the selling partner authorizes your application. For more information, refer to Authorizing Selling Partner API applications . No. Include refresh_token for calling operations that require authorization from a selling partner. If you include refresh_token , do not include scope. scope The scope of the LWA authorization grant. Values:

d0:b590.text: No. Include scope for calling a grantless operation . If you include scope, do not include refresh_token . client_id Get this value when you register your application. Refer to Viewing your developer information . Yes client_secret Get this value when you register your application. Refer to Viewing your developer information . Yes

d0:b591.text: Example for calling an operation that requires selling partner authorization:

d0:b593.text: POST /auth/o2/token HTTP/l.l Host: api.amazon.com Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8 grant_type=refresh_token &refresh_token=Aztr|... &client_id=foodev &client_secret=Y76SDl2F

d0:b594.text: Example for calling a grantless operation :

d0:b596.text: POST /auth/o2/token HTTP/l.l Host: api.amazon.com Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8 grant_type=client_credentials &scope=sellingpartnerapi::notifications &client_id=foodev &client_secret=Y76SDl2F

d0:b599.text: To avoid getting an untrusted certificate authority (CA) error when calling the LWA authorization server, be sure to update your trust store so that your application trusts the LWA authorization server.

d0:b600.text: A successful response includes the following values.

d0:b601.text: Name Description access_token The LWA access token. Maximum size: 2048 bytes. token_type The type of token returned. Must be bearer . expires_in The number of seconds before the LWA access token becomes invalid. refresh_token The LWA refresh token that you submitted in the request. Maximum size: 2048 bytes.

d0:b603.text: HTTP/l.l 200 OK Content-Type: application/json;charset UTF-8 Cache-Control: no-store Pragma:no-cache { "access_token":"Atza|IQEBLjAsAhRmHjNgHpi0U-Dme37rR6CuUpSREXAMPLE", "token_type":"bearer", "expires_in":3600, "refresh_token":"Atzr|IQEBLzAtAhRPpMJxdwVz2Nn6f2y-tpJX2DeXEXAMPLE" }

d0:b604.text: For more information, visit the Authorization Code Grant page in the Login with Amazon documentation.

d0:b606.text: An SP-API URI contains the following components.

d0:b607.text: Name Description Example HTTP method The HTTP method. GET Endpoint An SP-API endpoint . https://sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com Path Resource location. /catalog/2022-04-01/items/{asin} Query string The query parameters. ?marketplaceIds=ATVPDKIKX0DER Path parameter The path parameters. EXAMPLEASIN

d0:b611.text: Step 3. Add headers to the URI

d0:b612.text: Add headers to the URI that you constructed in Step 2. Construct a Selling Partner API URI . Here are the HTTP headers to include in requests to the SP-API:

d0:b613.text: Name Description host the Amazon store endpoint. Refer to SP-API endpoints . x-amz-access-token The LWA access token. Refer to Step 1. Request a Login with Amazon access token . Note about restricted operations. If you call a restricted operation, pass in an RDT here instead of an LWA access token. For information about getting RDTs and calling restricted operations, refer to the Tokens API Use Case Guide in the Tokens API Use Case Guide. x-amz-date The date and time of your request. user-agent Your application name, application version number, platform, and programming language. You must include a user-agent header in every request to the SP-API. • Maximum length: 500 characters. • Minimum required information: App name, version, and language. • Optional: You can add additional attributes separated by semicolons. How to assemble a user-agent header Concatenate the following information: • Application name • Forward slash • Application version • Space • Opening parenthesis • Language name/value pair • Closing parentheses Escape the following characters with a blackslash: • Backslash. • Forward slash in the application name. • Opening parenthesis in the application version. • Equal sign in the attribute name. • Closing parenthesis and semicolon in attribute values. Examples: • AppId/AppVersionId (Language=LanguageNameAndOptionallyVersion) • MySellingTool/2.0 (Language=Java/1.8.0.221; Platform=Windows/10) • MyCompany/build16 (Language=Perl; Host=my.desktop.example.com)

d0:b614.text: The following example shows how to call the SP-API with a URI and headers but no signing information:

d0:b616.text: GET /catalog/2022-04-01/items/EXAMPLEASIN?marketplaceIds=ATVPDKIKX0DER HTTP/1.1 host: sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com user-agent: My Selling Tool/2.0 (Language=Java/1.8.0.221; Platform=Windows/10) x-amz-access-token=Atza|IQEBLjAsAhRmHjNgHpi0U-Dme37rR6CuUpSREXAMPLE x-amz-date: 20190430T123600Z

d1:b575.text: You must register as a Selling Partner API (SP-API) developer before you can register your Selling Partner API application .

d1:b576.text: The procedure for registering as a developer varies slightly depending on the type of application that you plan to create:

d1:b577.text: Private seller applications : Applications for sellers that are available only to your organization, and are self-authorized. Note that in Seller Central, you must have a professional selling account to develop SP-API private seller applications. Individual accounts are not eligible. You can upgrade your account to a professional plan at any time.

d1:b578.text: Private vendor applications : Vendor applications that are available only to your organization, and are self-authorized.

d1:b579.text: Public seller and vendor applications : Applications that are publicly available and are authorized by sellers or by vendors using OAuth. In accordance with the Solution Provider Portal Agreement , public developers must list their app in the Amazon Selling Partner Appstore.

d1:b582.text: Public and private applications are subject to authorization limits and restrictions. For more information, refer to Authorization Limits .

d1:b583.text: You must be a primary account user to complete registration.

d1:b585.text: Before you register, review the following information:

d1:b586.text: Policy requirements: Review the Acceptable Use Policy (AUP), Data Protection Policy (DPP), and Solution Provider Portal Agreement at Policies and Agreements .

d1:b588.text: Ensure that the tech team responsible for data security answers the security control questions of the developer profile application.

d1:b589.text: Review the Selling Partner API technical papers for detailed guidance on vulnerability management, network protection, and data encryption.

d1:b590.text: To understand key security controls for SP-API integration and how these controls relate to DPP provisions, see Key Security Control Guidance .

d1:b591.text: Website requirements: If you are registering as a public developer or service provider, ensure that your website meets the Website Guidelines for Public Developers and Service Providers .

d1:b592.text: Role selection: To understand which roles to request, review Selling Partner API Roles .

d1:b593.text: Application guidelines: Keep your developer profile application under the 500-word limit and write original content. Do not copy information from the AUP, DPP, or other Amazon policies.

d1:b594.text: Status tracking: For information about your registration status, refer to Developer Registration Request Status .

d1:b595.text: Profile updates: To learn how to update your developer profile, refer to Update Your Developer Profile in Solution Provider Portal .
